assessments.reasoning: In the SPDX Data repository's GitHub API response, annotated object 76c9a79bb7d2bf851143b76b3935a4d7cbaa644b carries tag v3.29.0 and targets an object of type commit with SHA 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48. This is the exact revision in the 2.0 detail locator. The API identifies the tag as unsigned.

At the target commit, json/details/NLOD-2.0.json records licenseId NLOD-2.0, name “Norwegian Licence for Open Government Data (NLOD) 2.0” and isDeprecatedLicenseId false. Both crossRef[0].url and seeAlso[0] specify http://data.norge.no/nlod/en/2.0. The comments separately identify /nlod/no/2.0 as a translation.

The digest-bound Agency HTML at the corresponding HTTPS host and path identifies the 2.0 edition in the title and §10. It directly supports the publisher-edition side of the correspondence in its context role. The SPDX release record supplies membership evidence.

challenge.method: Traced v3.29.0 to the pinned 2.0 JSON and checked identifier, title, deprecation and both English reference fields. Compared host, language and edition path against the Agency originals. Tested substitution of the 1.0 edition, attribution to SPDX as licence publisher, use of the translation link and an inference of equivalent text.
challenge.results: The pinned references and the HTTPS original share data.norge.no/nlod/en/2.0. A change to /en/1.0 fails both the edition title and the sole-version provision. The translation comment has a distinct /no/ path. The Agency page identifies the publisher, while SPDX owns the generated detail. The recorded match value “false” gives no affirmative text-equivalence result.

limitations: The annotated tag is unsigned. This assessment establishes its recorded target and leaves signer authentication and the current mutable tag ref unverified.

The scheme difference establishes no HTTP redirect or byte equivalence. The evidence covers documentary correspondence at this Data revision. XML build lineage, text equivalence, Norwegian-language representation, compatibility and work-specific grants remain outside scope.
reasoning: The generated NLOD-2.0 detail at the annotated v3.29.0 target names the 2.0 licence and points to the Agency's English 2.0 edition. SCES §§4 and 7 require targeted review of significant cross-index relationships, a pinned owning-index revision and disclosure of what the external source establishes. The release object and detail establish what SPDX recorded. The publisher's version provision resolves which NLOD edition the reference identifies.
